Proportional-odds ordinal logistic regression

Source: R/ordinal_reg.R
ordinal_reg.Rd

Fit crude, exposure-specific adjusted, or joint multivariable proportional-odds models and return publication-ready common odds ratios.

Usage

ordinal_reg(
  data,
  outcome,
  exposures,
  adjust_for = NULL,
  multivariable = FALSE,
  multivariate = NULL,
  assumption_test = TRUE,
  model_stats = FALSE,
  format = c("flextable", "gt"),
  theme = "minimal",
  show_ref = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame containing the outcome and predictors.

outcome

An ordered-factor outcome. Its level order defines movement from lower to higher categories.

exposures

Predictor variables to report.

adjust_for

Optional covariates included but not reported.

multivariable

Logical; fit all exposures in one model.

multivariate

Optional alias for `multivariable`.

assumption_test

Logical; perform term-level likelihood-ratio tests of the proportional-odds assumption.

model_stats

Logical; return model-fit and sample-size statistics.

format

Output table format: `"flextable"` or `"gt"`.

theme

Table styling preset.

show_ref

Logical; display categorical reference rows.

Value

A `gtregression` object containing the publication table, fitted models, common odds ratios, proportional-odds tests, and metadata.

Details

An odds ratio above one indicates greater odds of being in a higher outcome category, assuming the proportional-odds assumption holds. The outcome must be an ordered factor so category direction is never inferred silently.

Examples

ordinal_data <- data.frame(
  recovery = ordered(
    c("Poor", "Fair", "Good", "Excellent", "Fair", "Good"),
    levels = c("Poor", "Fair", "Good", "Excellent")
  ),
  treatment = factor(c("Control", "Control", "New", "New", "Control", "New")),
  age = c(70, 64, 58, 51, 62, 55)
)
ordinal_reg(
  ordinal_data,
  outcome = recovery,
  exposures = treatment,
  adjust_for = age,
  assumption_test = FALSE
)
#> Warning: (1) Hessian is numerically singular: parameters are not uniquely determined
